explanation: Vapor barrier web at the main wheel well (BS 663, LBL 40) is wing-to-body structure; the text has no 'wing' word, so the model picks fuselage. Compare 513945: same location, coded 53.
The galley/aisle 'transition strip' carries floor-path emergency lighting (JASC 3350), but the text never mentions light; read as cracked floor structure.
'1L door low pressure' on the attendant panel is the door's emergency-opening cylinder (5210); slides and bottles are ATA 25, so 25 is a near miss.
Same wheel-well vapor barrier at STA 663 as case 511781, but this report is coded 53 while that one is 57: reporters disagree, so no model can be right on both.
Attendant flashlight test failure: this operator codes flashlights as emergency lighting (3350); others code them as cabin equipment (25).
Wear on the keel-beam hinge fitting of the MLG door is structure (53); the word DOOR pulls the prediction to 52.
Missing orange 'girt bar engaged' decal is a placard (ATA 11, mapped to OTHER); the model sees girt bar/slide vocabulary and predicts 25 with 0.99 confidence.
Cracks in the frame segments AROUND the overwing exit hatch are fuselage structure (53); 'EMERGENCY EXIT HATCH DOOR' points to doors (52).
Total loss of green hydraulic quantity is a hydraulic-power fault (29), which the model predicts; the report is coded 3130 (indicating/recording), possibly because a sensor was blamed.
'Dirty sock' smell is a fume event: the source can be the APU (49) or the packs (21). This is the known 49/21 confusion in the confusion matrix.
'Lower bezels' of the overwing escape: bezels are also typical of light fixtures (33), so the word alone is ambiguous; the true code is the overwing escape hatch (5220).
Gear retraction with a red nose-gear light is coded 5280 (landing-gear doors); 32 (landing gear) is a very plausible reading from the problem text alone.
Flight-deck door latch handle hard to rotate: most reporters would code doors (52), which the model predicts; this one is coded 5300.
Engine 2 EGT over limit: EGT faults are usually coded 77 (engine indicating, part of OTHER); this report uses 72, so the model's OTHER is a reasonable miss.
The problem text is only 'DUE TO THE MAJOR': Phase 3 cut the sentence 'DUE TO THE MAJOR REPAIR...' at REPAIR (an action verb), leaving no usable content.
Engine stuck at 70% N1 on takeoff roll could be fuel control (73), indicating (77) or engine (72); the model chooses the engine group OTHER, the report uses 72.
Cracked vertical FRAME beside the emergency exit is fuselage structure (53); EXIT/EMERGENCY pull the prediction towards doors (52).
The center wing box sits inside the fuselage and is coded 53 here, but the word WING pulls the prediction to 57.
Center wing box front spar at FR36: again fuselage-coded (5315) but described with wing vocabulary; the model predicts 57.
Corrosion on the fuselage pan around the APU inlet door is coded 4910 (APU); the model reads it as fuselage structure (53).
